root_idea.summary: The root has two distinct semantic axes: joy and gladness as the opposite of sorrow, and burdening or making heavily burdened.
root_idea.development: The affective branch describes an opening or lightness of the heart through delight, often especially immediate or worldly delight. A separate derived branch develops meanings of burdening, particularly through debt, alongside causative meanings of making joyful.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Form I verb citation form.
Displayed as the adjective فَرِحٌ, the useful citation form for the Quranic nominal occurrences.

senses.definition: To feel joy, gladness, or happiness; to rejoice.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic use denotes an experience of delight or gladness. The delight may be immediate and worldly, or may be directed toward a valued gift, outcome, or promise.

senses.definition: To exult or rejoice beyond measure.
senses.usage_conditions: In the explicitly blameworthy construction, the excessive rejoicing carries implications of insolence, ingratitude, or unthankfulness.
An adjectival description of a person or group experiencing joy or gladness, including joy directed toward what has been granted or received.

senses.definition: Well pleased or content with what one has.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ or an equivalent object of satisfaction to describe contentment with a possession, condition, or religious position.
In the Quranic condemnation of the الفَرِحِينَ, the adjective denotes excessive exultation associated with insolence and ingratitude.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be well pleased or content with a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct use of the verb alongside the ordinary sense of experiencing joy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone joyful, glad, or happy; to make someone content; or to cause someone to exult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative Form IV use covering the several degrees of producing joy, contentment, or excessive exultation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grieve someone or make someone unhappy, literally to deprive that person of joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary causative use documented alongside the meaning ‘to make joyful.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: To burden, burden heavily, or overburden.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a debt, an obligation, or a thing that weighs heavily upon someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Joy, mirth, gladness, or happiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A simple substantive for the state or sensation of joy; it is contrasted with sorrow and may denote transient delight rather than settled tranquillity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of being well pleased or content with a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the general state of joy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Exultation or rejoicing above measure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe excessive exultation accompanied by insolence, ingratitude, or unthankfulness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A festivity or merry-making, especially a marriage celebration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or contemporary conventional use of the noun for a celebratory occasion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the expression مِنَ الفَرَحِ, the word may be interpreted as مِنَ المَفْرُوحِ بِهِ, meaning the beloved or desired object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic interpretive use, not the ordinary abstract meaning ‘joy.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: A joy, gladness, or happiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A feminine noun for an instance or state of joy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or occasion of joy, gladness, or happiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A thing through which someone is made joyful or happy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gift or recompense given to someone who brings joyful news.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional reward for announcing good news, comparable to a congratulatory gift or good tidings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Reportedly, a white truffle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reading and root assignment are disputed in the cited lexical discussion; another transmission gives قُرْحَانَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person burdened heavily by debt, a fine, bloodwit, ransom, or a similar obligation and unable to pay.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also used for someone overcome by such liability in need of communal assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A needy or poor person, including one possessing no property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A related use describing someone overwhelmed by want or poverty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person not known to have kinsfolk or near relations.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported lexical use concerning a person without known familial support.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slain person found between two towns or villages.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reported use for an unidentified or unclaimed dead person found in an open area.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing, affair, or event that makes someone joyful, glad, or happy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word describes the cause of happiness, rather than the person experiencing it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular exhilarating medicine given to someone in grief so that they become happy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical medical designation, also called سُلْوَانٌ in the cited discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who rejoices much or often.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may describe someone who rejoices whenever fortune makes him happy.

Gift or recompense for joyful news.
Reported truffle meaning with a disputed reading.

cautions: The reported فَرْحَانَةٌ meaning ‘white truffle’ is textually disputed, since another transmission gives قُرْحَانَةٌ; it is retained as a qualified Classical report rather than treated as a secure central root meaning.
